name: Hereditary Neuropathy with Liability to Pressure Palsies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for HNPP

criteria.description: Recurrent, transient focal neuropathies triggered by minor trauma or compression
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Detection of PMP22 gene deletion or mutation by molecular genetic testing
Electrophysiological evidence of demyelinating neuropathy with conduction block
Tomacula formation on nerve biopsy (focal myelin thickenings)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent focal neuropathies plus either positive family history or confirmed PMP22 gene deletion/mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is considered the gold standard for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent focal mononeuropathies triggered by minor compression
Tomacula (focal myelin thickenings) on nerve biopsy

common.symptomName: Hypoesthesia or sensory loss in peripheral nerves
Foot drop due to peroneal nerve palsy

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy in chronically affected muscles
Pain or discomfort at sites of nerve compression

genetic: Deletion or mutation of PMP22 gene on chromosome 17p11.2
other: Nerve conduction studies showing demyelinating features and conduction block

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive distal muscle wasting rather than recurrent focal palsies
Progressive or relapsing course without clear trauma triggers

redFlags: Persistent or progressive weakness without recovery
Signs of systemic illness or inflammation
references: Lupski JR, et al. Hereditary Neuropathy with Liability to Pressure Palsies. GeneReviews. 2020.
Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of hereditary neuropathy with liability to pressure palsies. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
Bird TD. Hereditary Neuropathy with Liability to Pressure Palsies. GeneReviews. 2019.
